questions.part: Part 1. Reading — Passage 1 (The Development of the Courier Service)
questions.passage:
The Development of the Courier Service

In ancient times, runners, pigeons and riders on horseback were used to deliver messages. Before there were mechanized courier services, foot messengers physically ran miles to their destinations. To this day, there are marathons directly related to actual historical messenger routes. In cities today, there are often bicycle couriers or motorcycle couriers, but for products requiring delivery over greater distance networks, this may often include trucks, railways and aircraft. §1.

The same-day courier market expanded with the help of taxi companies, but soon expanded into dedicated motorcycle dispatch riders with the taxi companies setting up separate arms to their companies to cover the courier work. During the late 1970s small provincial and regional companies were popping up throughout the country. Today, there are many large companies offering next-day courier services, including worldwide couriers such as APC Overnight, FedEx, DHL, UPS and TNT. There are many "specialist" couriers usually for the transportation of items such as freight/palettes, sensitive documents and liquids. §2.

There are thousands upon thousands of independent couriers and localized companies, offering next-day and same-day services. Since the turn of the millennium, there has been a noticeable increase in owner-drivers, self-employed couriers, operating mainly from home with a sole vehicle. Advantages of this rather than working for an established same-day courier firm are that they are able to offer far better rates to their customers. Self-employed couriers come from varied employment backgrounds from non-skilled through to highly qualified tradespeople. Motorbike couriers still exist, but mainly in and around cities, where there is often congestion, as they are much cheaper to run in heavy traffic. §3.

Large couriers often require an account to be held (and this can include daily scheduled collections). Senders are therefore primarily in the commercial/industrial sector (and not the general public); some couriers such as DHL do, however, allow public sending (at higher cost than regular senders).

The courier industry has long held an important place in United States commerce and been involved in important moments in the nation's history, such as westward migration and the gold rush. Wells Fargo was founded in 1852 and rapidly became the preeminent package delivery company. The company specialized in shipping gold, packages and newspapers throughout the West, making a Wells Fargo office in every camp and settlement a necessity for commerce and connections to home. Shortly afterward, the Pony Express was established to move packages more quickly than the traditional method, which was the stagecoach routes. It also illustrated the demand for timely deliveries across the nation, a concept that continued to evolve with the railroads, automobiles and interstate highways and which has emerged into today's courier industry. §4.

The courier industry in the United States is a $59 billion industry, with 86% of the business shared by only four companies, including DHL, FedEx and UPS. The remaining 14% shared among almost 11,900 other small businesses ranging in size from 1 employee to over 600. These businesses comprise of mostly same-day deliveries and are strong offline businesses and strong online businesses like Naparex and USA Couriers.
questions.q: How did the courier market expand?
options: with the help of cab companies
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 states: "The same-day courier market expanded with the help of taxi companies" — a cab company is a taxi company.

Early Football

Documented evidence of what is possibly the oldest activity resembling football can be found in a Chinese military manual written during the Warring States Period in about the 476BC-221BC.

(1)____ During the Han Dynasty (206BC-220AD), cuju games were standardized and rules were established. Variations of this game later spread to Japan and Korea, known as kemari and chuk-guk respectively. By the Chinese Tang Dynasty (618-907), the feather-stuffed ball was replaced by an air-filled ball and cuju games had become professionalized, with many players making a living playing cuju. Also, two different types of goal posts emerged. (2)____

The Ancient Greeks and Romans are known to have played many ball games, some of which involved the use of the feet. The Roman writer Cicero describes the case of a man who was killed whilst having a shave when a ball was kicked into a barber's shop. The Roman game harpastum is believed to have been adapted from a team game known as pheninda that is mentioned by Greek playwright, Antiphanes (388-311BC) and later referred to by Clement of Alexandria. (3)____

There are a number of references to traditional, ancient, and/or prehistoric ball games, played by indigenous peoples in many different parts of the world. (4)____ There are later accounts of an Inuit game played on ice, called aqsaqtuk. (5)____ In 1610, William Strachey of the Jamestown settlement, Virginia recorded a game played by Native Americans, called pahsaheman. In Victoria, Australia, indigenous people played a game called Marn Grook ("ball game"). An 1878 book by Robert Brough-Smyth, The Aborigines of Victoria, quotes a man called Richard Thomas as saying, in about 1841, that he had witnessed Aboriginal people playing the game: "Mr Thomas describes how the foremost player will drop kick a ball made from the skin of a possum and how other players leap into the air in order to catch it." (6)____

A. One was made by setting up posts with a net between them and the other consisted of just one goal post in the middle of the field.
B. They often look much different in different places.
C. This game appears to have resembled rugby.
D. It is widely believed that Marn Grook had an influence on the development of Australian football.
E. Each match began with two teams facing each other in parallel lines, before attempting to kick the ball through each other team's line and then at a goal.
F. Although this is true only in certain societies.
G. For example, in 1586, men from a ship commanded by an English explorer named John Davis went ashore to play a form of football with Inuit (Eskimo) people in Greenland.
H. It describes a practice known as cuju (literally "kick ball"), which originally involved kicking a leather ball through a hole in a piece of silk cloth strung between two 30-foot (9.1 m) poles.

questions.q: "Do you think Greg was at the gym on Sunday?" "He _____. It's closed on weekends."
questions.explanation: Can't have been expresses a confident deduction about the past that something was impossible: the gym is closed on weekends, so he could not have been there.

questions.q: The mayor announced his plan _____ a new library.
questions.explanation: The noun plan is followed by for + noun phrase: "a plan for the construction of a new library". "To be constructed" would wrongly make the plan itself the thing being built.

questions.q: The state of the economy is poor. _____, the unemployment rate is rising.
questions.explanation: Two separate sentences need a linking adverb, not a conjunction or preposition: Consequently (= as a result) introduces the effect of the poor economy.

questions.q: Do you know what time it is? You _____ to be here an hour ago!
questions.explanation: Be supposed to + infinitive expresses what was expected or arranged; the past passive form "were supposed to be here" is required with "an hour ago".

questions.q: I've been buying all my clothes from second-hand stores _____.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous describes a recent habit, which goes with lately (= recently). "Today" and "all day" describe a single day, not a repeated action.

questions.q: The fantastic view was _____ me to buy this apartment.
questions.explanation: A nominal relative clause with what (= the thing that) completes the sentence: "The fantastic view was what convinced me to buy this apartment."

questions.q: Dean has two sisters, both _____ work abroad.
questions.explanation: After a comma, "both of" + relative pronoun joins the two clauses; the object form whom is required after a preposition. "Both of them work abroad" would need a full stop or "and".

questions.q: Magie didn't seem _____ concerned when Jack told her about the snake in her bedroom.
questions.explanation: Not the least bit + adjective means "not at all": she didn't seem the least bit concerned. "At least" has a different meaning (a minimum).

questions.q: I've made my decision. _____ you say will change my mind!
questions.explanation: Nothing you say will change my mind: the subject is "Nothing (that) you say", and the sentence must be negative to fit "I've made my decision". "Whatever" would give a positive meaning.

questions.q: Bob _____ as a baggage handler at the airport until he can find something more suitable.
questions.explanation: The present continuous is working describes a temporary situation, signalled by "until he can find something more suitable".

questions.q: Although not everyone is a fan of Justin Bieber, most people agree he is worthy of his _____ success.
questions.explanation: Phenomenal success is a fixed collocation meaning extraordinary, remarkable success.

questions.q: My brother _____ a total transformation during adolescence.
questions.explanation: Undergo a transformation means to experience a change; "underwent" is the past form.

questions.q: There is _____ parking for both staff and customers.
questions.explanation: Ample parking means more than enough parking space; the other adjectives do not collocate with "parking".

questions.q: A therapist is trying to help the couple _____ with the strain of the situation.
questions.explanation: Cope with means to deal successfully with something difficult, here "the strain of the situation".

questions.q: William _____ to becoming a powerful politician and has already started to make his way in the world of politics.
questions.explanation: Aspire to + V-ing/noun means to have a strong ambition to achieve something: he aspires to becoming a powerful politician.

questions.q: Will you _____ all these books and papers to my office, please?
questions.explanation: Take is used for carrying something away from the speaker to another place ("to my office"); "bring" means carrying it towards the speaker.

questions.q: "Is Leah OK?" "Yes, we spent hours _____ about her problem and she seems to feel better now."
questions.explanation: Talk about something is the natural collocation; "discuss" takes a direct object without "about", and "listen" goes with "to".

questions.q: You will find the stockbrokers' offices in the city's central _____ district.
questions.explanation: Central business district (CBD) is the fixed term for the commercial centre of a city, where stockbrokers' offices are found.

questions.q: I stayed up all night because I was completely _____ the book I was reading.
questions.explanation: Be absorbed in something means to be so interested in it that you notice nothing else, which explains staying up all night.

questions.q: You'll have to reverse out of this road – it's a _____ and we can't go any further.
questions.explanation: A dead end is a road that is closed at one end, so you cannot go any further and must reverse.

questions.q: Her _____ success at the polls is the best indicator of her popularity.
questions.explanation: Unprecedented success means success never seen before; "unabridged" describes texts, "unrequited" love, and "unrelenting" pressure or effort.

questions.q: The little boy was _____ by the storekeeper, who charged him twice the normal price for a soda.
questions.explanation: Rip someone off means to cheat someone by charging too much, as the storekeeper did by doubling the price.

questions.q: Jackie lives on the fourth floor of a _____ in London's West End.
questions.explanation: Only a block of flats has a fourth floor; a bungalow is single-storey and houses do not usually have four floors.

questions.q: I'm sure your cat will soon get used to her new _____.
questions.explanation: The plural noun surroundings means the environment or place around you; "get used to her new surroundings" is the standard phrase.

We consume wine, beer, cider, spirits… in fact, the (0) fermented product of almost anything we can turn into alcohol. Our (1)____ for this toxic substance, the cause of so much trouble, is something of a mystery. Maybe it is enough to say that we drink because it makes us feel good. But to understand our love of alcohol we need a bigger, more (2)____, explanation.

The story of alcohol is one of an intimate relationship between humans and yeasts, an affair that began millions of years ago and is still playing out today. We like to cast ourselves as the star of this drama, but in fact yeasts are the (3)____ lead character. Ours is a symbiotic connection – a mutually beneficial (4)____. It is also one in which the balance of power is constantly shifting. If anything, the yeasts seem to have had the (5)____ hand, at least since our ancestors began brewing their own grog. We cultivate yeasts, ensuring they survive and thrive, and in return we get, at best, a good night out and a (6)____ the next morning. Once upon a time, however, yeast and alcohol may have offered us more (7)____ rewards.

Today the costs of our love of alcohol often (8)____ any benefits. But, being a story of evolution, it doesn’t end there. Already some humans have acquired (9)____ changes that encourage them to drink less. If this trend continues, it is possible that one day this long and (10)____ relationship will reach a kind of tenuous truce.

0. FERMENT · 1. FOND · 2. EVOLVE · 3. SING · 4. PARTNER · 5. UP · 6. HANG · 7. SIGNIFY · 8. WEIGH · 9. GENE · 10. TEMPEST
questions.q: We cultivate yeasts, ensuring they survive and thrive, and in return we get, at best, a good night out and a (6)____ the next morning. (HANG)
questions.explanation: A noun after "a … the next morning": a hangover is the headache and sickness felt after drinking too much alcohol.
